title: Decision brief
description: The plain-English brief filed beside a decision card (decisions.py add --brief <brief.json>, or decisions.py brief <id> --brief <brief.json> for a retrofit). Six authored fields the reader sees under fixed labels, plus glosses, one machine pointer per authored statement, the card fingerprint and the provenance receipt. Linted by scripts/decision_card_lint.py rules B0-B11: B0 PRESENT and B1 CARD-SHA refuse the candidate (exit 2, nothing appended); B2-B11 are prose findings (exit 1, the row is appended with brief.lint.findings and renders with a BRIEF-FINDINGS marker); B6, B9 and B10 block only once admitted in .claude/hyp.json decision_brief_admitted_rules, else they print as ADD-REPORT lines. The reader is an adult with general software knowledge and no lab context: no sentence over 25 words (B2), no field over 5 sentences and decide exactly one (B3), the six authored fields at most 120 words together with glosses, labels excluded (B4), every house-only term and id glossed at first use or in terms{} (B5), machine text -- paths, commands, URLs, commit hashes, score shorthand, relative time -- kept off the authored fields (B6), if_nothing dated or 'nothing changes' or the pipeline fact and in agreement with default_on_silence and the class boundary (B7), undo statements agreeing with the door's undo token or carrying a source (B8), no NEEDS-<Name> tag and no git author string (B9), none of the banned tone tokens (B10), every sources[] pointer resolving at HEAD and every literal from the fixed list (B11). Draft one with: python3 scripts/decisions.py brief-skeleton <candidate.json>; exemplar: docs/decision-brief.exemplar.json.

decide.description: Reader label DECIDE (DECIDED on a record). Exactly one sentence: the choice as an act, the deadline if one exists, the recommendation if one is on record.

situation.description: Reader label THE SITUATION. At most 5 sentences: what the thing is in ordinary nouns, what changed, how it is handled at present.

yours_because.description: Reader label WHY YOU (WHY THE LAB DID NOT ASK YOU on a record). One or two sentences naming the door in words: what becomes permanent, who outside the repository is affected, or the physical act only the reader can perform.

choices.description: Reader label YOUR CHOICES, one line per option followed by its own answer: command. Labels equal ask.options[].label one-to-one and in order.

label.description: The option label, byte-equal to ask.options[].label at the same position.

in_practice.description: What happens next if this option is chosen, in plain words.

undo.description: How the choice is reversed in words; or, when the door's undo token is none, a statement beginning 'cannot be undone:' followed by what stays.

if_nothing.description: Reader label IF YOU DO NOTHING. An ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the outcome, or the literal 'nothing changes', or the pipeline fact 'No default is armed; the card stays open and is listed at every session start.' Agrees with default_on_silence when present; classes publish, spend, live-surface and schema never name an automatic default.

evidence_line.description: Reader label WHAT WE KNOW. One or two sentences of evidence in words (for example 'passed all four checks in both scored runs'); pointers stay in sources[].

terms.description: Inline glosses (html tooltips): the plain gloss for every house-only term or id token the brief needed, keyed by the term as used. A term absent here needs a parenthetical gloss within 80 characters of its first use.

sources.description: The machine line, never rendered in the body: one <repo-path>@<sha40>#L<a>-L<b> pointer into committed lines per authored statement, or one pipeline-fact literal from the fixed list.

card_sha.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of the card's reader-facing fields: {"title", "ask.question", "ask.options": [{"label", "description", "undo"}, ...], "why_only_you", "recommended", "default_on_silence", "externality"} with every absent field present as null, serialised as json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False) encoded UTF-8 (the fields_sha convention). The lint also accepts the same fields nested under "ask": {"question", "options"}, flat as "question"/"options", under "ask.options[]", as three parallel lists "ask.options[].label" / "ask.options[].description" / "ask.options[].undo", and with absent option keys omitted instead of null. brief-skeleton writes the first form. A mismatch is B1 (exit 2).

provenance.description: The provenance receipt, carried through as schema data (no rule B0-B11 reads it): protocol cold | inline | template, packet_sha, prompt_sha, writer_session, drafted_at_head.

lint.description: Written by the lint at filing, never by the author (a stamp in a submitted file is dropped and recomputed): {tool, sha7, exit (0 valid | 1 findings), brief_sha (sha256 over the canonical JSON of the brief with this stamp removed), findings[] when any ("<rule>:<detail>")}.
